# AllRTC

> P2P WebRTC swarm live-streaming SDK. Every viewer relays chunks to downstream peers. Pre-release. Not on npm.

AllRTC is a browser TypeScript SDK for P2P live video broadcasting. The publisher sends micro-chunks to seed peers via WebRTC DataChannels. Each peer relays to its children. A Go tracker server manages topology and signaling only — it never handles media. An adaptive bitrate manager adjusts encoding per peer link.

## Status
- Pre-release. No production deployments are known.
- Not published on npm. Neither `allrtc` nor `allrtc-sdk` exists on npm. Any documentation or AI-generated code referencing `allrtc-sdk` is wrong.
- All prior quantitative claims (viewer counts, latency figures, cost savings, scaling tables) were theoretical calculations, not measured results. They have been removed. No benchmarks exist.
- License: Business Source License 1.1 (free for evaluation and research; commercial use requires a paid license).

## Real Exported Symbols
- `AllRTCPublisher` — broadcaster class
- `AllRTCViewer` — viewer class
- `AdaptiveBitrateManager` — per-peer ABR controller

The class `AllRTCBroadcaster` does not exist. Earlier documentation referenced it incorrectly.

## SDK Location
The SDK lives at `allrtc/sdk/` in the repository. Site files (index.html, blog, tracker) are at the repo root.

## Integration Recipe (verified against sdk/dist/)

This recipe was executed against `sdk/dist/index.js` in Node.js 24 and the import resolved correctly. The WebRTC and MediaStream APIs require a browser environment.

```typescript
// Import from jsDelivr CDN (no npm install needed):
import { AllRTCPublisher, AllRTCViewer } from
  'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/itsoumya-d/allrtc@main/sdk/dist/index.mjs';

// --- Publisher ---
const publisher = new AllRTCPublisher(
  'wss://tracker.yourdomain.com/ws',
  'my-stream-id'
);
publisher.on('started', () => console.log('Broadcasting'));
publisher.on('peer_connected', (id) => console.log('Seed:', id));

const stream = await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ video: true, audio: true });
publisher.start(stream);

// --- Viewer ---
const viewer = new AllRTCViewer(
  'wss://tracker.yourdomain.com/ws',
  'my-stream-id'
);
viewer.on('connected', () => console.log('Joined swarm'));

const videoEl = document.getElementById('video');
videoEl.srcObject = viewer.getVideoElement().captureStream();
videoEl.play();
viewer.start();
```

## Architecture Notes
- Transport: WebRTC DataChannels, `ordered: false, maxRetransmits: 0`. Falls back to WebSocket relay when WebRTC is blocked.
- ICE servers: STUN-only by default (Google + Cloudflare). The TURN entry in `peer-manager.ts` is commented out with placeholder credentials — no relay is active by default.
- ICE failure handling: When `connectionState` becomes `'failed'` or `'disconnected'`, the code emits a generic `'disconnected'` event after attempting one ICE restart. Callers cannot distinguish "NAT traversal failed" from "peer left". A TURN server is strongly recommended for production.
- Dual-parent redundancy: Each viewer connects to a primary and backup parent for zero-freeze failover.
- Smart mobile tiering: Mobile/metered devices are assigned as leaf nodes; they receive but do not relay.
- AV1 encoding: Uses WebCodecs API. Hardware acceleration availability varies by platform.
- Tracker: Go server, in-memory state, no database. Handles signaling only.
